question_text: Following the use of alcohol or drugs, no person shall act as a flight crew member

subject: General / Human Factors
learning_objective: State the hazard of flying with a head cold.

choices.label: A
choices.text: is always safe while taking antihistamine tablets.

choices.label: D
choices.text: can cause a prolonged infection of the middle ear.

explanation: A cold can block the Eustachian tube, preventing pressure equalization in the middle ear during altitude changes, which can cause a prolonged middle-ear infection or barotrauma.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Antihistamines carry their own aeromedical concerns (drowsiness) and do not make flying with a cold 'always safe.'
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Flying does not clear sinus congestion; pressure changes can worsen sinus/ear blockage.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: There is no blanket 'safe below 5,000 ft' exception; altitude-related pressure changes are a concern even at lower altitudes.

subject: General / Human Factors
learning_objective: State the effective collision-avoidance scanning technique.
question_text: Effective collision avoidance scanning technique requires

choices.label: A
choices.text: a series of regularly spaced eye movements focusing for at least one second on each block area.

choices.label: B
choices.text: a continuous sweeping motion scanning back and forth along the horizon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: concentrating on a distant object to prevent the eyes from focusing nearby on an empty field of vision.

choices.label: D
choices.text: an up and down sweeping motion cutting the horizon at a 30° angle.

explanation: The recommended technique uses a series of short, regularly spaced eye movements, pausing at least one second on each sector/block area, rather than a continuous sweep.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: A continuous sweeping motion is less effective than discrete, paused segments, since the eyes need to stop briefly to focus and detect small/distant targets.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: This describes an attempt to counter empty-field myopia, not the standard scanning pattern itself.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: A fixed 30-degree up/down sweep is not the standard recommended horizontal block-scanning technique.
